subject: maths
question: A common internal tangent for two circles measures 18 cm. The distance between the centers of these circles is 30 cm. If the larger circle has a radius of 16 cm, what is the radius of the smaller circle?
solution:
**Given:**

Length of common internal tangent = 18 cm

Distance between centers (d) = 30 cm

Radius of larger circle (R) = 16 cm

Radius of smaller circle = r cm

**Formula used:**

(Internal tangent)² = d² − (R + r)²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f554250aceb775a47256b704d08ffbee671622fd6cf7c019b3f401fe357e664e.png] 

⇒ 18² = 30² − (16 + r)²

⇒ 324 = 900 − (16 + r)²

⇒ (16 + r)² = 900 − 324

⇒ (16 + r)² = 576

⇒ 16 + r = 24

⇒ r = 24 - 16

⇒ r = 8 cm

**∴ Radius of the smaller circle = 8 cm.**
